item.title: Building Products, Understanding Customers
item.description: I’ve built a paid investment education community and now lead technical review and acceptance for Jobdream, whose AI-agent platform serves marketplace sellers. My work starts with understanding what people need and taking responsibility for what gets delivered.

item.title: What Remains Valuable When Answers Become Cheap?
item.description: I built an investment education audience on YouTube, grew it beyond 9,000 subscribers, and offered a private Telegram community at $30 a month. As AI became better at explaining concepts, I began questioning what I should continue to offer. That question now follows me into game development and engineering work for a merchant-agent platform.

item.title: About Me
item.description:
Current Work

Technical Lead — AI Architecture & Engineering Delivery

Jobdream · Consulting engagement

Guide technical direction for Jobdream’s platform, which uses AI agents to help small marketplace businesses manage their operations, working with external engineering teams.

  • Evaluate engineering vendors and review proposed system architecture against product requirements.
  • Review pull requests and external engineering teams’ implementations for reliability, security, maintainability, and alignment with the intended agent architecture.
  • Make technical acceptance decisions on outsourced deliveries and identify issues to address before production deployment. The CEO retains final business approval.

Founder — Investment Education Community

  • Built a YouTube audience that peaked above 9,000 subscribers and remains above 7,500 as of September 2026.
  • Offered a private Telegram community at $30/month, sharing investment perspectives and teaching members to use code to explore investment questions.
  • Reduced activity as I reconsidered the value of the offering in light of increasingly accessible AI tutoring.

item.title: Exploring Dollar-Cost Averaging with Python
item.description:
Archive note: This tutorial was written in October 2021. Its dataset, examples, external data-download instructions, and reported results reflect that period.

Introduction

Dollar-cost averaging (DCA) means investing a fixed amount at regular intervals, regardless of the asset’s price. This is the definition used by Investor.gov. In this tutorial, we use Python to explore how this approach performed over a historical Bitcoin price sample.

This is a historical coding exercise, not an investment recommendation. The results describe one sample period, not expected future returns.
